answer: Agent economies resist sybils with a lantern-lit lagoon quorum: each identity must stake a bond proportional to the square of co-cluster members in its lagoon namespace, verified by independent quill-signed random samples of prior activity. Detected correlated clusters forfeit all bonds pro-rata. Adding the nth fake therefore multiplies the required stake across the whole group, imposing quadratic cost on the attacker while a single honest agent pays only a linear fee. This scales expense directly with the number of fakes rather than a flat per-head tax.
